DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

18 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When there are no signs, signals, or police at an intersection, what does the law say?

options.text: Drivers on the right must yield to drivers on the left.
There is no law about who must yield.
Drivers going straight must yield to drivers turning left.
Drivers turning left must yield to drivers going straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers turning left must yield to drivers going straight.
questions.explanation: When there are no signs, signals, or police, drivers turning left must yield to vehicles going straight through the intersection.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line. What does this tell you?

options.text: You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines can be crossed to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: When can you turn left on a red light?

options.text: When there is no oncoming traffic.
When you turn from a two-way street onto a one-way street.
When you turn from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
When the car in front of you turns left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you turn from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: You can turn left after stopping at a red light if you are on a one-way street in the left lane and turn onto another one-way street. A sign may prohibit this turn. You must stop first and yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. What must you do?

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
Tell the other vehicle to pull over.
Turn on your high beams so they see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles coming toward you at least half of the road space. Both vehicles need enough room to pass safely.

questions.question: A transit bus is signaling to return to the main road after a stop. What must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to any transit bus that is signaling to enter the main road after loading or unloading passengers. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus merge safely.

questions.question: When should you leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopping?
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the vehicle ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, extra space helps prevent a collision.

questions.question: The light is green and you want to turn left, but oncoming traffic is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for the traffic to pass before you turn. If the light is green and no vehicle ahead is turning left, you can move into the intersection to prepare for your turn.

questions.question: How should you prepare to handle situations on the road ahead?

options.text: Look at the entire road and the sides of the road.
Stare straight ahead at all times.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and the sides of the road.
questions.explanation: Your ability to handle dangerous situations depends on spotting problems early. Look ahead and also scan the entire road, including the sides. Do not just stare at the center of the road.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in this state?
questions.explanation: The maximum speed limit in Pennsylvania is 70 mph.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: The condition of the road greatly affects your ability to stop. You must slow down when roads are slippery or in poor condition. Driving too fast on poor roads puts you at risk if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: A solid line on the road edge shows where the road ends. If the line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends. Traffic must merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends. Traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane on a multilane road ends ahead. Cars in the right lane must move left.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, look left first because traffic from the left is closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to catch any traffic you may have missed.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Traffic only moves in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic only moves in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A one-way sign tells you that traffic flows only in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.question: Who has the right-of-way at intersections?
questions.explanation: The law does not give anyone the right-of-way. It only says who must yield. Even if another driver must yield, you still need to stop or move to avoid a crash.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any train coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to stop for a train at railroad crossings. Do not cross until your whole vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: How many minutes does the average person need to process one drink of alcohol?
questions.explanation: The average person needs at least 60 minutes to process one drink.

questions.question: If a car coming toward you has high beams on, look toward ____ of the road.
questions.explanation: If a car coming toward you has bright high beams, look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you stay on your path until the car passes.
